objective: Produce app/rotation.py exposing exactly the four C1 functions and tests/test_rotation.py in which every C1/C3 behavior (naming, rotation decision, live-file rename, 7-file retention, compress-older-than-yesterday) passes against tmpdir fixtures with an injected now: datetime — observable: pytest tests/test_rotation.py -q fully green and git diff shows changes only in the two owned paths.

concepts: ISO timestamp prefix parsing (%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S) for the live log's last line
date math with datetime.date: yesterday = now.date() - timedelta(days=1); compress iff D < now.date() - 1
gzip module round-trip; one retention slot per dated file (plain or gz, one artifact per date)

inputs: Frozen contract C1 (inlined below): exact signatures and semantics of app/rotation.py
Frozen contract C3 (inlined below): naming, retention, and compression policy

frozen_contracts.spec: app/rotation.py exposes exactly: rotation_name(d: date) -> str — returns 'app-' + d.strftime('%Y%m%d') + '.log'; needs_rotation(last_date: date | None, now: datetime) -> bool — True iff last_date is not None and last_date < now.date(); rotate(log_dir: Path, now: datetime) -> Path | None — live file is log_dir/'app.log'; determine its date from the ISO timestamp prefix of its last line (fallback: file mtime date; empty/missing file: no rotation); if that date < now.date(), rename the live file to rotation_name(that date) and return the new Path, else None; apply_retention(log_dir: Path, now: datetime, keep: int = 7) -> list[Path] — for each rotated file app-YYYYMMDD.log with date D < now.date() - 1 day: gzip it to app-YYYYMMDD.log.gz and delete the plain file; then over all dated rotated files (plain and gz, one slot per date) sorted by date descending, delete everything beyond the first `keep` and return the deleted paths. The module imports only stdlib (pathlib, datetime, gzip, re) and nothing from app/ or tests/.

Log file naming and retention policy: live file = logs/app.log; rotated file = logs/app-YYYYMMDD.log named after the completed day (date of the live log's last line); compressed = logs/app-YYYYMMDD.log.gz; at most 7 dated rotated files retained (a gz file occupies the same date slot as its plain file; after successful compression the plain file is deleted, so at most one artifact per date); a rotated file with date D is compressed when D < now.date() - 1 day (today's rotated file and yesterday's stay plain-text).

non_goals: Do not touch app/logger.py or app/server.py (owned by T02 / unmodified per S2)
Do not implement any LogWriter wiring or trigger points (that is T02)
No background thread, timer, or cron — the module is pure functions called by the writer (DA-NO-TIMER)
No writing under the real logs/ directory — tests use tempfile.TemporaryDirectory only
implementation_constraints: Python 3.11 stdlib only: pathlib, datetime, gzip, re — no other imports in app/rotation.py
All four functions take now: datetime as an explicit parameter — the module never reads wall-clock time
The module must not import anything from app/ or tests/ (C1; prevents the S1 import cycle)
Tests follow the style of tests/test_log.py: unittest, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, injected now, zero wall-clock dependence
Explicit encoding='utf-8' on all text file reads/writes

deliverables.what: Rotation policy module implementing C1 exactly (four public functions, no other exports)
Unit tests for naming, decision, rotate, retention (A3), compression (A4)

acceptance_tests.description: rotation_name(date(2026, 9, 8)) == 'app-20260908.log' for at least three dates across a month boundary (e.g. 2026-08-31, 2026-09-01, 2026-09-08).
needs_rotation(D, now on D) is False; needs_rotation(D, now on D+1) is True; needs_rotation(None, now) is False for any now.

Live app.log with last line dated D and now = D+1: rotate() renames it to app-<D>.log and returns that Path; live file is absent afterwards. Same-date now → None and file untouched. Empty live file → None.
A3: nine rotated files dated today-1 .. today-9; apply_retention(now=today, keep=7) deletes exactly today-8 and today-9, returns both deleted Paths, and exactly 7 dated files remain.
A3 negative: with fewer than 7 rotated files, apply_retention deletes nothing and returns [].

A4: rotated file dated today-2 is gzipped to app-<today-2>.log.gz, the plain file is deleted, and gzip.decompress of the gz equals the original bytes; pre-existing gz (idempotent re-run) leaves content unchanged and still deletes the plain file.
A4 negative: rotated files dated today-1 (and today, if present) remain plain-text after apply_retention.
A3 failure behavior: files not matching app-YYYYMMDD.log(.gz) (e.g. app.log, notes.txt, app-2026-09-08.log with dashes) are ignored by the retention pass — never renamed, compressed, or deleted.

failure_cases.scenario: Live log's last line has no parseable ISO timestamp prefix (corrupt line)
failure_cases.expected_behavior: rotate() falls back to the live file's mtime date (C1 fallback); if that date < now.date(), rotation proceeds with the mtime date.

failure_cases.scenario: Live file is empty or missing
failure_cases.expected_behavior: rotate() returns None without error; no rotation.

failure_cases.scenario: gz target already exists for a rotated file
failure_cases.expected_behavior: apply_retention deletes the plain file without rewriting or corrupting the existing gz (idempotent).

failure_cases.scenario: Log directory contains unrelated files alongside rotated files
failure_cases.expected_behavior: Only names matching the app-YYYYMMDD.log(.gz) pattern are ever compressed or deleted.

handoff.notes: app/rotation.py is complete against C1/C3: exactly four public functions, no other exports, no app/-imports, no wall-clock reads. All tests run in tmpdir with injected now. No file outside app/rotation.py and tests/test_rotation.py was touched. T02 imports the four functions by their C1 names.
